newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Quiet Australia stocks nudge higher by noon.
newsitem.headline: Quiet Australia stocks nudge higher by noon.

text.p: *Stocks little moved to midday, some options trade but little interest pre-ANZAC Day long weekend. Volume 123.08 million, value A$285.93 million, 828 traded, 290 steady, 280 up, 258 down.
The Australian share market slumbered its way through a slow morning session to register thin gains by midday with investors taking a cautious stance ahead of the holiday weekend.
Australian markets will be closed on Friday for ANZAC Day.
By 12.05 p.m. (0205 GMT), the benchmark All Ordinaries index was up 3.7 points at 2,476.0.
June share price index futures were up eight points at 2,485, a nine point premium to the index.
Traders said most of the volume had been generated by today's April series option expiries with investors reluctant to commit ahead of the long weekend.
"If it wasn't for options there would be a lot less volume than there is," said dealer Phillip Toop of Lance Jones, suggesting that the afternoon session would also be lethargic.
"I think people will be winding back a bit this afternoon into the long weekend," he said, noting that U.S. markets had another two trading sessions before Australian markets reopened.
Rises slightly shaded falls, while about 35 percent of stocks traded remained steady.

In other local markets, Australian bond yields moved higher as the market attempted to consolidate Wednesday's post-CPI data sell-off. By 12.15 p.m. (0215 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.88 percent, up from Wednesday's 7.83 percent.

The Australian dollar had another indecisive session as failures in both directions offshore reinforced the strength of the recent range with local morning trade also failing to provide any direction.
By 12.15 p.m., the local dollar had drifted to US$0.7750/55 from US$0.7777/82 late here Wednesday, and was still stuck in the week's US$0.7730/7795 range.
